headline: High-risk shared filesystem and browser-driven interaction create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; Taipy’s local-only network posture limits exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code post-tool events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, while taipy has no documented isolation or provenance controls. That creates a plausible path where ctx-written content is later consumed as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF ctx writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or MCP channel that taipy later reads as instructions
IF taipy ingests file content without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic instruction parsing from shared files
Add provenance tags to any handoff files
Review shared MCP/file inputs before execution
requires-engineering: enforce content-type or schema validation on handoff channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers, and has filesystem access; taipy is documented as local-only network egress none. A shared workspace could still expose sensitive ctx data to taipy outputs or UI, even if taipy cannot exfiltrate externally. The blast radius is multiple work products, so medium fits.
conditions: IF ctx and taipy share a filesystem or workspace
IF taipy renders or logs ctx files containing audit/runtime logs or graph data
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Restrict taipy to read-only access on shared inputs
Redact logs before handoff
Turn off any automatic file preview in taipy
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and filesystem writes, while taipy is a data-engineering app with no concurrency controls documented. Overlapping writes to the same workspace can corrupt files or state even without explicit network access. Because locking is not documented, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or mutable dataset
IF no external lock or orchestrator serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize write operations manually
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Keep one agent read-only during the other’s write phase
requires-engineering: add transactional or lock-based coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can generate context and logs that taipy may consume in downstream data workflows, and taipy is a scheduler/data-engineering tool that may act on inputs without human verification. That makes A-to-B propagation plausible in default use, though not directly evidenced. The pair therefore presents a medium cascading-error risk.
conditions: IF taipy uses ctx-produced files or logs as authoritative inputs
IF taipy triggers jobs or transformations without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a manual review step before taipy actions
Require schema validation on ctx outputs
Mark ctx outputs as advisory only
Log source provenance in taipy pipelines
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and graph data, which can carry retention or residency obligations, while taipy’s profile does not document any conflicting compliance posture. No direct mismatch is evidenced, so only a low compliance risk is supportable from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF ctx logs or graph data contain regulated personal data
IF taipy stores or displays those same records under a different retention policy
mitigations: Classify data before sharing
Avoid placing regulated data in shared logs
Set a short retention window
Document the handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
